items.summary: Bank Danamon Indonesia President Director Nobuya Kawasaki says Indonesia’s economy remains resilient despite concerns over the country’s outlook, pointing to strong loan demand and consumer activity. He speaks with Haslinda Amin from the sidelines of 'Singapore Fintech Festival 2026'. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Ripple’s Garlinghouse Sees Crypto Assets Diverging
items.summary: Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse expects crypto assets to increasingly diverge in performance, with utility and real demand separating winners from more speculative tokens. He remains bullish on the industry despite a difficult year for the broader crypto market. He speaks with Haslinda Amin from the sidelines of 'Singapore Fintech Festival 2026'. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Tech outages are piling up, and AI is raising the stakes. Could this be the new normal? - The Washington Post
How Trump Is Approaching the Xi-Putin Trilateral
items.summary: Reporting live from Shenzhen, Bloomberg's Stephen Engle explains how US President Donald Trump has emphasized a stable relationship and personal rapport with Chinese President Xi Jinping ahead of their bilateral meeting at the APEC summit in Shenzhen. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Lores Says AI Commerce Is an Opportunity for PayPal
items.summary: PayPal President & CEO Enrique Lores says the shift toward AI-driven, agentic commerce is an 'incredible opportunity' for the company, with trust, security and identity becoming increasingly important. He also discusses PayPal’s turnaround, expansion into financial services and investment in AI. Lores speaks with Haslinda Amin from the sidelines of 'Singapore Fintech Festival 2026'. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Anthropic Shares Indicated About 20% Higher on Gray Market
items.summary: Anthropic PBC shares are indicated to open between 20% and 26% higher in gray market trading after the artificial intelligence lab’s upsized $107.3 billion initial public offering and private placement broke SpaceX’s record.

items.title: Lenovo Shares Tank After Posting First Operating Loss Since 2017
items.summary: Lenovo Group Ltd. reported a far larger-than-anticipated loss for the September quarter, reflecting accounting charges and the mounting cost of PC components. Its shares plunged more than 13%.
